challengerRole: C-Team challenger: independent re-read of every issue plus source-tree verification
method: Every issue re-read from `gh issue view <n>`; every family slug checked against families.md; every cited source directory and named .ts file checked with ls/glob; every representative function name checked with rg for a real `export`.

structuralValidation.note: proposals.json is structurally sound: 122 unique issues, contiguous #1592-#1713, every primary and secondary slug exists in families.md, and every proposed package matches the issue's own pkg:* label (122/122). The defects are semantic, not structural.

familyVocabularyProblems.detail: families.md names `functions/src/typed/poly.ts`, which does not exist. Real homes: functions/src/typed/algebra.ts (polyval, line 218), functions/src/typed/interpolation.ts (polyFit, line 506), functions/src/algebra/polynomialRoot.ts and functions/src/wasm/poly/.
`communityColoring` does not exist in functions/src. functions/src/graph/community-coloring.ts exports graphColoring, maxClique, louvainCommunities, katzCentrality, isIsomorphic.
`envelope` has zero occurrences in functions/src (case-insensitive grep). It is a *gap* the issues ask for, not an existing function - listing it misreads the tree.

`hannWindow` and `blackmanWindow` do not exist. functions/src/signal/windows-extra.ts exports kaiserWindow, gaussianWindow, tukeyWindow, blackmanHarrisWindow, nuttallWindow, flattopWindow, bohmanWindow, parzenWindow, plus a name-keyed constructor accepting hann/hamming/blackman (windowFunctionCore, functions/src/signal/spectral-segments.ts).

Representatives `convmtx`, `xcorr2`, `cconv` have zero definitions in functions/src - they are #1695 gap rows. The family also attributes fft2d to functions/src/signal/fft.ts when it is in typed/signal.ts.

`magic`, `gallery`, `rosser` do not exist (they are #1705 gap rows). `hilbert` exists only as `hilbertMatrix` (functions/src/linalg-special-matrices.ts:26). The structure predicates have exactly one in-tree implementation, `isSymmetric` at matrix/src/operations/common.ts:176 - neither cited file.

Claims det/inv entry points in matrix/src/operations, but that directory has no det.ts or inv.ts (only condest.ts, pinv.ts). det/inv/trace/diag are mathjs factories in functions/src/matrix/{det,inv,trace,diag}.ts. The slug is also referenced by NO proposal, so the only family covering the matrix package is unused.

Claims "sparse support in operations/"; matrix/src/operations has no sparse file. SparseMatrix is matrix/src/types/SparseMatrix.ts (fromCOO/getCSR), and the CSparse port is functions/src/algebra/sparse/.

Names `functions/src/ml/gaussian-process.ts`; functions/src/ml holds only dbscan-knn, glm, kde, logistic-regression, ols, regularized-regression. The GP code is functions/src/stats/gaussian-process.ts.

Names functions/src/numeric/gauss-nodes.ts, which exports only rootsLegendre. The Chebyshev/Hermite/Laguerre/Jacobi nodes are gauss-nodes-extra.ts (rootsChebyshevT, rootsChebyshevU, rootsHermite, rootsLaguerre, rootsJacobi). polygamma-orthopoly.ts mentions Chebyshev only in a comment; chebyshevT/hermiteH/laguerreL are typed functions in functions/src/typed/special.ts.

Representative `reduce` resolves to functions/src/typed/algebra.ts:1729 `export function reduce(expr: string): string` - the CAS Reduce (Wolfram Reduce), not a list fold. The list-ish implementations are the factories createMap/createFilter/createForEach/createReduce in functions/src/matrix/.
Claims haversine (real home functions/src/geometry-extra.ts) and cart2pol/cart2sph (real implementation is `coordinateTransform` at functions/src/typed/geometry.ts:565) for the trigonometry family.

One family bundles three unrelated subsystems: Mathematica per-number precision tracking (Precision/Accuracy/SetPrecision), interval arithmetic (IntervalUnion/Intersection/MemberQ/CenteredInterval) and machine-constant queries ($MachineEpsilon/$MaxNumber/eps/realmax). 29 rows with no shared implementation surface; interval arithmetic already has its own module at functions/src/numeric/interval.ts.

Both families list functions/src/fit-scalar.ts as a source dir, so one file belongs to two families. Conversely curve-fitting lists curvefit and levenbergMarquardt, which live in functions/src/typed/numeric.ts and functions/src/optimization-extra.ts - neither is listed.

Three families claim the same ufunc surface: isclose/allclose/clip and elementwise max/min appear under array-selection, all/any appear under array-reductions, and arithmetic.elementwise claims the whole "ufunc completion" concept. The issue lists overlap too: numpy.where + select/nonzero appear in #1608 and #1612; all/any in #1608, #1609 and #1708; isinf in #1607, #1608 and #1707.
Lists `solveODE (numeric counterpart)` as a representative function; solveODE belongs to functions.ode, so the row points readers at the wrong family.

Both are correctly marked proposed, but #1671-#1675 explicitly propose a new package `@danielsimonjr/mathts-image` with its own entry point. The vocabulary is package-scoped to `functions`, so the model cannot record the intended package; the same would apply to a future finance entry point.

"62 families across 13 packages" gives arithmetic/trigonometry/statistics/signal/linalg/units/numbers their own package rows even though they are thin re-export packages with a single index.ts, while CAS (~7 families), geometry, graphs, control, PDE, image and finance all sit under the single `functions` row. `functions` therefore carries 31 families while its eight peer re-export packages carry 1-10 each. A reader cannot tell whether a family means "the functions package" or "an implementation home that some thin package re-exports".

entries.evidence: The convenience classes span all six numpy.polynomial series: Polynomial (power basis), Chebyshev, Legendre, Laguerre, Hermite, HermiteE. Four of six are orthogonal series; existing orthogonal-series code is functions/src/numeric/gauss-nodes-extra.ts (rootsChebyshevT/U, rootsHermite, rootsLaguerre) and typed/special.ts (chebyshevT/hermiteH/laguerreL). functions/src/typed/poly.ts, which families.md cites, does not exist.
entries.counter_proposal: Arguable that primary should be functions.orthogonal-polynomials with secondary functions.polynomials, since domain/window mapping and convert/cast are orthogonal-series concepts. Either order is defensible.
entries.note: Unsure because the base Polynomial class is power-basis, so the worker's ordering is not wrong - only its cited source dirs are.
